newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy looking to accelerate GDP growth in H2-Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy looking to accelerate GDP growth in H2-Prodi.

text.p: The Italian government hopes to consolidate the country's fledgling economic recovery and speed up growth in the winter months, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday.

"We want to accelerate this recovery after the summer, because as it stands (the recovery) is not sufficient to lower unemployment," Prodi told reporters. "The aim is not for some abstract recovery, but a recovery in employment."

Italian gross domestic product (GDP) in the first quarter fell by 0.4 percent year-on-year and slipped 0.2 percent over the fourth quarter of last year, but state-funded economic research institute Isco said in a report this week that the economy is likely to have grown in the second quarter of 1997.
Isco added that the phase of stagnation which characterised 1996 and the start of 1997 could now be considered to be over.
"The recovery is still young, but it is (definitely) a recovery which we will have to consolidate," Prodi said.
The government has forecast GDP growth of around 1.2 percent this year.
